text:
alex: Heads-up — I kicked off a long-context repro that consistently triggers KV cache spill/handoff fragmentation and steady RSS growth. Putting notes + repro here.

maya: thanks, can you share the exact command and config?

alex: sure — basic repro command below (ran on a 4xA100 node):
```
./kvcache_benchmark \
  --model=llama2-13b \
  --seq_len=16384 \
  --kv_reuse=true \
  --workload=interleaved_long_context \
  --batch_policy=auto \
  --duration=2h \
  --memprof=true
```

alex: quick summary of what I observed in the first run: RSS slowly climbs from ~1.2GB to ~6.3GB in ~45m. Fragmentation counters show free_segments drop from ~120 -> ~18 while avg_segment_size shrinks (16KB -> ~3KB). System-level swapping not triggered but eviction rate increases and tail latency spikes.

jon: ugh that matches the flakiness I saw last week on the emberload suite. Might be eviction threshold logic + handoff behavior.

maya: does toggling kv_reuse change anything?

alex: yes — disabling --kv_reuse stabilizes RSS at ~1.5GB but at the cost of ~2x token latency. So it's definitely tied to reuse/hand-off codepath.

kevin: can you paste a short profiler snippet (heapstats / segment table)?

alex: pasted a trimmed snippet from memprof output:
```
[00:10:12] total_nodes: 15234
[00:10:12] free_segments: 120
[00:55:30] total_nodes: 15234
[00:55:30] free_segments: 18
[00:55:30] avg_segment_size: 3072
[00:55:30] rss: 6_345_000_000
[evictions/1m]: 340 -> 1200
```

alex: also saw KV reuse counters show many small allocations during handoff (lots of <4KB fragments). Seems compaction isn't running or isn't effective during the burst.

perf-bot: created regression test: kvcache/long-run/spill-handoff-1789990001 — CI job queued (link: https://ci.redwood/queue/3782) :gear:

jon: another datapoint: when batch_policy forces batch_size >= 8 we see more churn — probably because larger batches trigger bigger temporary KV allocations and force handoff more often. Could be kernel selection as well (some kernels allocate temporary KV buffers).

kevin: idea — add a lightweight compaction pass on handoff if free_fragments below threshold, and raise the micro-eviction threshold so we don't evict tiny segments eagerly. Pseudopatch: 
```
if (handoff && free_fragments < FRAG_LIMIT) {
  compact_kv_segments(); // coalesce tiny fragments
}
if (evict_batch_size < MIN_EVICT) evict_batch_size = MIN_EVICT;
```

maya: sounds reasonable. Any perf/risk tradeoffs? compaction could add CPU during handoff and briefly lengthen p99.

alex: agreed — but compare p99 hit vs 4GB permanent RSS growth. I can run the regtest with compaction enabled overnight across 6 seeds and collect heap profiles + per-token latency.

kevin: also check kernel selection logs — if a different matmul kernel path leads to temporary KV allocations, we should prefer the kernel that reuses buffers. Add a kernel-selection flag to reproduce.

alex: noted. I'll toggle kernel_preference=stable_buffer in the next run as well.

jon: thanks — also tag @kevin in the CI job so infra can allocate longer runtime if needed.

perf-bot: CI job updated: added long-run timeout (4h) and artifact retention 7d.

alex: plan: run compaction + raised eviction batch + kernel_preference=stable_buffer across 6 runs tonight, will upload memprof traces + per-token latency histograms to the regtest artifacts. If we see memory stabilize and acceptable p99 increase (<10%), we'll open a PR.

alex: will update when runs finish — thanks all :rocket:
